name: Salvador Fidalgo to Valdez
summary: Sent from the new Spanish post at Nootka to watch the Russians, Salvador Fidalgo sails the San Carlos into the Gulf of Alaska. In Prince William Sound he takes possession for Spain and names Puerto Córdova and Puerto de Valdés, the Valdez and Cordova of today, then visits the Russian posts on Cook Inlet and Kodiak. Cook had charted these coasts in 1778, and Spain kept its own charts in its archives, so the voyage added little to what the world knew; its names are what remain.
